content: If you want to become full, let yourself be empty. If you want to be reborn, let yourself die.
author: Lao Tzu
story:
There is a sharp, grounded clarity in this observation. Reminding yourself of your mortality is not morbid; it is the most clarifying lens available to human consciousness. When you remember that your days are strictly numbered, petty resentments and trivial anxieties evaporate.

Lao Tzu understood that real peace is never won by escaping the world or blaming external circumstances. Death gives urgency and sweetness to every ordinary afternoon. Because this day will never come again, the way you spend your attention right now is of monumental significance.
reflectionPrompt: In what relationship or encounter can you practice seeing beyond outer masks into shared humanity?
